alt: Poster: Sensex +905 pts (+1.24%) to 74,151, Nifty 50 22,936.75 (+1.05%), Midcap/Smallcap 100 about +1%, 29 Oct 2026
text:
Indian equities snapped a two-day losing streak on 29 October, with the Sensex rising over 900 points.

• The Sensex closed at 74,151, up 905.01 points (about 1.24%), per Business Standard and NewsBytes.
• The Nifty 50 closed at 22,936.75, up 237.90 points (about 1.05%), per Business Standard and India TV (previous close 22,698.85).
• Nifty Midcap 100 rose about 0.99% and Nifty Smallcap 100 about 0.95%, per Business Standard; NewsBytes also reports both up roughly 1%.
• Most sectors ended higher, with Nifty Realty the top sectoral gainer; Nifty Auto was the only loser, per Business Standard.

Our view: the rise was broad rather than confined to a few heavyweights, which is a better-quality signal than a narrow index move. Still, one session after a two-day fall says little about direction, and press reports continue to flag elevated crude and a weak rupee as variables. This is an interpretation of the data, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: after a sharp one-day rebound, do you look first at breadth or at institutional flows to judge whether it can hold?
